threads.body: [General] `fromSuppliedConnectOptions` copies the options but discards their endpoint group. Since stable extraction now reads only `getConfiguredServerAddress()`/`getConfiguredServerPort()`, all supplier/deferred queries still omit stable `server.address` and `server.port`, contrary to this PR's stated behavior. Build a `VertxSqlAddressGroup` from the copied options and update the stable/duplicate-semconv assertions (including concurrent trace ordering).

replies.body:
No code change.

Analysis: This comment targets VertxSqlClientData.fromSuppliedConnectOptions, which is not present at the pinned pull request head. The current flow captures each supplied SqlConnectOptions during the connection attempt and creates VertxSqlClientInfo through VertxServerTarget.from(...). The supplier assertions cover server.address and server.port in the default, stable, and duplicate semantic convention modes, including sorted concurrent query traces. No code change is needed.

Upsides: Keeping the current implementation avoids reintroducing the obsolete data model while preserving the configured target on supplier and deferred queries.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: [Javaagent] These weak caches attach instrumentation state to individual third-party connection, command, and future instances. Repository guidance requires typed `VirtualField`s for this lifecycle instead of external `Cache<Object, ...>` side tables; keep each field with the instrumentation that knows the concrete carrier (the existing version-aware command virtual-field registration can be extended).

replies.body:
No code change.

Analysis: The weak caches described in this comment are not present at the pinned pull request head. VertxSqlClientSingletons uses VirtualField handles for command contexts and connection metadata. VertxSqlClientInstrumentationModule registers both Vert.x 5.0 and 5.1 carrier class names with their exact value types. The remaining virtual fields use concrete library carrier types such as Pool, SqlClientBase, PreparedStatement, and ClientBuilderBase. No code change is needed.

Upsides: Keeping the current implementation follows the repository's per-object state guidance and preserves version-specific carrier registration without adding duplicate storage.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: [Testing] Repository test guidance explicitly disallows `database/dup` tasks (`.github/instructions/java-tests.instructions.md:73-77`). Please keep the existing default and stable tasks only, and remove the duplicate-mode-only assertion branches added for this task.

replies.body:
Addressed in 547190520d3cdbb046ba360a1b64e7cef32d294f.

Analysis: The added testBothSemconv task runs the database/dup mode even though repository guidance limits database semantic convention tests to the default and stable modes. The four special assertion branches exist only for that unsupported task. I removed the task and branches while retaining the shared default and stable assertions.

Upsides: The module now follows repository test policy, keeps the check lifecycle focused on supported modes, and removes assertion code that no supported test task uses.

Downsides: The module no longer has explicit duplicate-mode coverage, which is intentional under the repository policy.
